Optimization and Control.title: Structural conditions on trust-region radius updates. Part I: first-order convergence and complexity
Optimization and Control.summary:
Trust-region methods differ chiefly in how they update the radius, and each rule has traditionally been analysed on its own terms. We show that three structural conditions on the radius sequence suffice: a lower bound relative to the gradient norm, a contraction on unsuccessful iterations, and a controlled expansion on successful ones. A mechanism is weakly admissible if it satisfies the first two, and strongly admissible if it satisfies the first and third.
  Strong admissibility yields the optimal worst-case complexity $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ for first-order stationarity, and extends global convergence to model Hessians growing linearly with the iteration; weak admissibility gives $\lim_{k\to\infty}\|\nabla f(x_k)\| = 0$ under uniformly bounded model Hessians. Both hold for every rule in the class, so a new mechanism is covered by verifying two inequalities rather than by a fresh convergence proof.
  We verify admissibility for five mechanism classes (fixed-factor, step-driven, retrospective, criticality-anchored and gradient-scaled), prove convergence of the retrospective update under linearly growing model Hessians, and extend the Lyapunov framework of Curtis and Scheinberg (2020), Wang and Yuan (2022) to three distinct scaling factors with decoupled step acceptance, covering $η= 0$; its stochastic version specialises to the deterministic gradient-scaled rule.
  Part II treats the asymptotic behaviour of the radius and convergence to second-order critical points.

Optimization and Control.title: Solving Classes of Linear Programs with Strongly Polynomial Straight Line Complexity in Strongly Polynomial Time
Optimization and Control.summary:
Recently, Allamigeon, Dadush, Loho, Natura, and Végh (ADLNV, SICOMP 2025) introduced an interior point method for linear programs whose number of iterations is bounded by the so-called straight line complexity (SLC) of the instance. This yields a strongly polynomial bound on the number of iterations of the corresponding interior point algorithm for broad classes of linear programs. In particular, in the companion paper we give a strongly polynomial straight line complexity bound for two-variable-per-inequality linear programs. However, in order to obtain a strongly polynomial algorithm for these classes, one also needs to address two important technical issues: initialization and bit-complexity bounds. Standard IPM initialization techniques either require numerical estimates that cannot be obtained in the strongly polynomial model, or involve modifying the instance in ways that do not preserve the geometry of the original LP, potentially affecting the SLC.
  In this work, we present an initialization framework for interior point methods for linear programming, along with a rounding procedure that ensures the continued feasibility of the IPM. We develop a multistage scheme in which each stage can be initialized in strongly polynomial time given the output of the previous stage. Additionally, we address the challenge of controlling the bit complexity of each iterate throughout the algorithm. To this end, we show that it is possible to represent iterates as low-complexity convex combinations of vertices and extreme rays. Our combinatorial rounding step is independent of the algorithm in ADLNV 2025, and can be applied more broadly in the context of path-following methods.
Optimization and Control.comment: This paper is based on the STOC 2024 proceedings paper "A strongly polynomial algorithm for linear programs with at most two nonzero entries per row or column'' , and includes the full details of the initialization framework and the bit complexity arguments

Optimization and Control.title: Attention's forward pass and Frank-Wolfe
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the hardmax limit of self-attention dynamics for token embeddings obtained in the zero-temperature ($β\to+\infty$) regime, and relate it to the finite-$β$ setting. In this limit, the update rule can be viewed as a Frank-Wolfe step for a quadratic objective over the convex hull of the current token embeddings. When the key-query matrix is negative semidefinite, the method linearly contracts all tokens to a single cluster at the origin. When it is positive semidefinite, extending the hardmax rule to the entire convex hull induces a Voronoi diagram: vertices are stationary, interior points remain in their initial cells, and each token moves along a straight line toward its cell's vertex, yielding (super-)exponential convergence. As a byproduct, we also establish well-posedness of the associated ODE limit in this regime. Returning to the finite-$β$ regime, we model self-attention dynamics as a Markov chain and prove dynamic metastability: with high probability, interior tokens reach near-vertex configurations in a constant number of steps and remain within a small neighborhood for times that grow exponentially in the inverse temperature $β$, before ultimately collapsing to the origin. Thus, the hardmax dynamics accurately approximate the finite-$β$ process over exponentially long time horizons.

Optimization and Control.title: Sum-of-Squares Certificates for Copositive Matrices via Recursive Identities: The de Klerk-Pasechnik Conjecture and Hoffman-Pereira Matrices
Optimization and Control.summary: We establish the conjecture by de Klerk and Pasechnik (2002), claiming that the semidefinite bounds $\vartheta^{(r)}(G)(r\geq 0)$ for the stability number $α(G)$ are exact at $r=α(G)-1$, by exhibiting an explicit sum-of-squares certificate. This certificate allows us to recover a known characterization of the minimizers of the Motzkin-Straus formulation for $1/α(G)$. Additionally, we give sum-of-squares copositivity certificates for the matrices satisfying the Hoffman-Pereira sign condition, a crucial condition for characterizing copositive matrices with $\{-1,0,1\}$ entries.
Optimization and Control.comment: Some typos and references have been corrected

Optimization and Control.title: Single-level reformulations for network pricing under Wardrop equilibrium with separable affine costs
Optimization and Control.summary:
We consider the problem of setting tolls on a subset of the arcs of a congested network so as to maximize the revenue of a network authority, anticipating that users route according to a Wardrop equilibrium. This problem is naturally cast as a bilevel program in which the leader sets tolls while the followers respond by choosing an equilibrium routing.
  We focus on the important special case of separable affine arc cost functions. Under this assumption, Wardrop equilibria admit Beckmann's convex characterization, from which we derive three new single-level reformulations of the bilevel problem, exploiting both Beckmann's formulation and its dual: an arc-based formulation, which we solve exactly, and two path-based formulations, solved by column-and-constraint generation. Beyond the reformulations, we further derive from Beckmann's potential an upper bound on the optimal revenue that can be used to certify optimality gaps across all formulations.
  An extensive computational study on instances derived from the Sioux Falls and Eastern Massachusetts networks compares our formulations with the recent mixed-integer nonlinear formulation of Beck, Labbé and Schmidt. The arc-based formulation solves substantially more instances to proven optimality (within a time limit of 1800 s) than this formulation and, unlike it, returns a feasible solution on every instance. It remains effective on the largest, 74-node network, on which the formulation of Beck et al. solves none. The magnitude of the upper bounds on the tolls proves to be a major driver of tractability: the genuinely hard core of the benchmark emerges once the regulatory cap on tolls is removed. The two path-based formulations, used as heuristics, return a solution within one percent of the optimum on every instance whose optimal value is known, often in seconds where exact formulations reach the time limit.

Optimization and Control.title: Acceleration Survives Heavy Tails and Generalized Smoothness
Optimization and Control.summary: We establish high-probability accelerated convergence guarantees for convex $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth optimization with unbiased stochastic gradients under heavy-tailed noise, assuming a central $α$-th noise moment bounded by $σ^α$, $α\in(1,2]$. Such guarantees are known under classical $L$-smoothness, but extending them through localization over an $O(R)$-radius ball may introduce an $e^{O(L_1R)}$ factor. We avoid this dependence in two ways. First, a two-phase scheme uses Clip-SGD to reach a low-curvature regime, after which clipped stochastic similar triangles (Clip-SSTM) attains, with probability at least $1-δ$, $f(y_K)-f^\star\le\widetilde{\mathcal O}\big(L_0R^2/K^2+σRK^{-(α-1)/α}\big),$ where $R$ bounds the distance from the Phase-II starting point to a minimizer. Second, a modified deterministic weight schedule allows Clip-SSTM to start directly from the initial point, controlling the high-curvature transient before recovering acceleration. With the prescribed initialization, both approaches recover the classical accelerated rate, with $L_1$ confined to an accuracy-independent transient, up to logarithmic factors. The two-phase analysis uses two coupled potentials to preserve the low-curvature regime despite momentum; the one-phase analysis controls the initial high-curvature regime using a modified version of the classical SSTM weight schedule.

Optimization and Control.title: Universal Learning of Nonlinear Dynamics
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the fundamental problem of one-step prediction of a marginally stable unknown nonlinear dynamical system. We describe an algorithm for this problem, based on the technique of spectral filtering, which learns a mapping from past observations to the next based on a spectral representation of the system. Using techniques from online convex optimization, we prove vanishing prediction error for any nonexpansive nonlinear dynamical system with finitely many marginally stable modes, with rates governed by a novel quantitative control-theoretic notion of learnability. The main technical component of our method is a new spectral filtering algorithm for linear dynamical systems, which incorporates past observations and applies to general noisy and marginally stable systems. This generalizes the original spectral filtering algorithm to both asymmetric dynamics as well as incorporating noise correction, and is of independent interest.

Optimization and Control.title: Topological entropy of nonlinear time-varying systems
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the topological entropy of nonlinear time-varying systems. We establish conditions under which entropy is independent of the initial time and derive two general upper bounds based on the matrix measure of the system Jacobian and the spectral abscissa of a Metzler comparison matrix, respectively. A general lower bound is also obtained using the trace of the Jacobian. For interconnected systems, we first derive an upper bound using the matrix measure of an interconnection matrix constructed from the Jacobian blocks. We then establish a new upper bound based on the spectral abscissa of a Metzler comparison matrix, incorporating the interconnection structure through subsystem-wise trajectory-separation analysis. This bound also recovers the two general upper bounds as special cases. All bounds depend on asymptotic properties of the Jacobian over reachable sets or their convex hulls. Simple examples show that either general upper bound may be tighter, while a time-varying Lorenz system illustrates the effects of norm selection and subsystem decomposition.

Optimization and Control.title: Distributed Algorithm for Linear Least Squares Problems via Iteratively Preconditioning by Successive Over-Relaxation
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper focuses on a novel distributed optimization algorithm for solving multi-agent linear least squares problems within a server-agent framework. Distributed methods are particularly suited to large-scale systems. The computational tasks can be partitioned across agents, while local data of one agent remain inaccessible to others. The proposed approach employs an iterative preconditioning scheme with the successive over-relaxation technique, leading to a substantial reduction of the number of iterations required for convergence, which presents a critical advantage where server-agent communication is costly. Theoretical convergence proof of the proposed algorithm is presented. Finally, benchmark problems are tested to demonstrate the performance comparison of the proposed approach over several prominent distributed methods.
Optimization and Control.comment: Accepted for publication in 2026 IEEE CDC

Optimization and Control.title: The Exact Boundary of Linear Optimality in Witsenhausen's Counterexample
Optimization and Control.summary: Witsenhausen's counterexample has resisted a closed form solution for decades. However, it has remained unknown whether a mathematically tractable representation exists or not. In this paper, we solve this open problem, showing that the optimal policies are either linear or not tame and characterizing the exact regions where the two properties hold. Moreover, in the linear optimal region, we give an essentially unique closed form solution for the optimal policy, and show that no optimal first-stage policy is definable in any $o$-minimal expansion of the ordered real field in the nonlinear optimal region.

Optimization and Control.title: Resonant Microstructures as Dirac-type Sources for Acoustic Wave Control
Optimization and Control.summary: We study finite-time acoustic wave tracking using effective interior Dirac-type actuators generated by clusters of subwavelength resonant bubbles driven from exterior transducers. Starting from a time-domain point-interaction approximation, the full scattering problem is reduced to a finite-dimensional delayed system of interacting retarded monopoles. After localization to a bounded observation domain, we formulate the tracking problem on a prescribed finite-dimensional Dirichlet spectral subspace. At the ideal level, a full-rank spatial coupling condition yields exact tracking of arbitrary sufficiently smooth compatible trajectories in this subspace by interior point sources. These ideal actuators are realized using small, high-contrast bubbles, whose Laplace-domain transfer operator encodes the Minnaert resonances and collective attenuation. The principal mode of each cluster is isolated by the Perron--Frobenius structure and the intra-cluster spectral gap. Clusters tuned to the same band are then treated as a collective resonant block. The selected Dirichlet bands are matched with the corresponding Minnaert bands. For prescribed slowly time-modulated resonant pressure profiles, with sufficiently flat initialization, we construct causal exterior controls and obtain a quantitative tracking estimate on every fixed time interval $[0,T]$. In contrast, on frequency ranges uniformly separated from the Minnaert resonances, the actuator gain is $O(\varepsilon)$ and the corresponding realization cost is asymptotically unbounded as $\varepsilon \ll 1$, $\varepsilon$ being the maximum radius of the bubbles. Thus the Minnaert resonances convert accessible exterior excitations into robust effective interior controls.
Optimization and Control.comment: The title of the manuscript has changed slightly. There are also updates to the proofs of some theorems/lemmas or propositions. Keywords. Wave equation; Effective Dirac actuators; Finite-time trajectory tracking; Causal control; Resonant microstructures; Minnaert resonance; Perron-Frobenius theory; Schur reduction; Matrix-block realization

Optimization and Control.title: Computation of Free Boundary Minimal Tori via Extremal Steklov Eigenvalues
Optimization and Control.summary: Fraser and Schoen showed that the first Steklov eigenfunctions of a metric maximizing the length-normalized first eigenvalue of a surface with boundary define a free boundary minimal immersion into a Euclidean ball. We develop a method for this extremal problem on surfaces of genus one with $b$ boundary components and use it to compute free boundary minimal tori for $b \in \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8\}$. By uniformization, the problem is a nonsmooth maximization over the modulus of a flat torus, the centers and radii of $b$ removed disks, and a boundary weight. The eigenvalues are computed with doubly periodic layer potentials, all derivatives follow from a single formula for the underlying pencil of boundary integral operators, and the coalescence of eigenvalues at a maximizer is handled by a two-stage nonsmooth method. The Lagrange multiplier matrix that certifies first-order stationarity rescales the eigenfunctions into the free boundary minimal immersion. For $b=1$, the supremum is the Fraser--Schoen bound $4π$, attained by branched double covers of the disk; the embedded torus with connected boundary of Carlotto, Franz, and Schulz is a saddle point, which answers their question whether it maximizes the eigenvalue in the negative. For $b \geq 2$ the largest values correspond to free boundary minimal tori in \mathbb{B}^5 and \mathbb{B}^6; the surfaces of Folha, Pacard, and Zolotareva, two disks joined by a central neck and $b$ equatorial necks, are maximizers within their symmetry class but saddle points of the full problem, with values increasing toward $4π$ as $b \to \infty$.

Optimization and Control.title: A Benders decomposition approach for hierarchical k-medoids
Optimization and Control.summary: We study a hierarchical clustering problem formulated as a sum of k-medoids objectives. This problem is related to the multi-period p-median problem, but instead of having nested facilities, we consider a hierarchy of nested assignments. We present two Benders formulations from the p-median literature and show how the obtained nested p-median solutions can be converted into hierarchical k-medoids solutions. We validate our methods on various instances. First, we show on small-scale instances that a standard Benders decomposition approach achieves speedups of up to three orders of magnitude over an existing branch-and-price method, while producing hierarchical k-medoids solutions that are at most 5% away from optimality. Second, we present an aggregated Benders heuristic that can handle instances with more than 13,000 observations.

Optimization and Control.title: Deep Stochastic Residual Methods for Fully Nonlinear Parabolic Equations
Optimization and Control.summary: We develop and analyze neural stochastic residual methods for fully nonlinear parabolic terminal problems under exact diffusion sampling. A quadratic stochastic residual supports global training and backward regression with scalar networks and losses involving only spatial derivatives. For global training, the correction removes a Hessian penalty from the limiting first-order loss. Under a uniform output regularity budget, we bound the continuous residual norm by the square roots of the global loss or normalized backward-regression excess loss, an $O(h^{1/2})$ discretization term for time step $h$, and terminal error. Residual stability then gives value, gradient and Hessian error bounds. Under suitable solution and terminal assumptions, we construct admissible networks with $O(h^{1/2})$ bounds on these approximation errors and the square roots of both loss criteria. In ten-dimensional backward-regression tests using a shared schedule tuned for the quadratic residual, mean relative Hessian errors are $5$--$6\%$ with the quadratic residual and about $15\%$ with the first-order residual. Tuned backward regression achieves Hessian accuracy comparable to physics-informed neural networks across the tested nonlinear coefficients. Translation tests show that the ratio of Hessian error to residual can grow sharply under a fixed sampling law.

Optimization and Control.title: Corrected Block Sparse Spectral Optimization: Exact Models, Finite Identification, and Local Dynamics
Optimization and Control.summary: The block generalized-power method pairs threshold-based support selection with inexpensive Stiefel updates, but the standard block formulation conflates two nonequivalent objectives and leaves inactive components, threshold ties, and post-selection refitting ill-specified. We rebuild the model from the primal. Eliminating each loading column from the normalized loading-ball problem gives a sum of soft-thresholded Euclidean norms (A-SUM); the squared-threshold objective in common use arises from a quadratic lift (A-SQ). We prove both identities, exhibit a two-component instance whose maximizers disagree, and specify explicit conventions for zero-response columns, ties, rank deficiency, and mask-before-refit. For A-SQ we separate the historical full-polar iteration from a safeguarded Riemannian ascent and prove, for the latter, whole-sequence convergence via a sufficient-ascent lemma, a relative-error lemma, and the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property, which applies because the soft-threshold objective and the Stiefel constraint are semi-algebraic. A strict threshold margin then forces finite identification of the support and sign pattern. The post-identification map is ordinary power iteration on the active covariance for a rank-one hard threshold, and the Frechet derivative of a coupled polar map for component-specific supports; a radius-based safe-screening rule follows from the same local analysis. Planted-spike experiments match the predicted identification time and local rates. On modern-AI panels (GPT-2 residual stream, ViT CLS stream, Pitprops) the thresholded block-sparse components match dense PCA on reconstruction and improve on it in monosemanticity and class specialisation. On three native-label scRNA datasets (Zheng17 FACS-sorted PBMCs, 68k donor-A with FACS-correlated labels, Tabula Muris) A-SQ beats dense PCA on cluster-recovery AMI by +0.023 to +0.044 at matched sparsity.

Optimization and Control.title: Kernel-based collocation methods for Zakai equations
Optimization and Control.summary: We analyze kernel-based interpolation methods for numerical solutions of Zakai equations in nonlinear filtering. The stability of the spatial discretization is quantified by row sums of the discrete differential operators. The resulting mean-square error estimate separates the one-step consistency error from its finite-time amplification and yields convergence when these two quantities balance. A short finite-resolution example illustrates the performance of a postprocessed interpolant.
Optimization and Control.comment: The corrected version of the paper published in Stochastics and Partial Differential Equations: Analysis and Computations (2019), Vol. 7, 476-494

Optimization and Control.title: A Unifying View of Distributionally Robust Optimization for Probability Smoothing via Maximum Entropy
Optimization and Control.summary: The probability smoothing problem seeks estimators that assign positive probability to all categories, including those unobserved in a finite sample. In our previous work, we established that the estimator derived from distributionally robust optimization (DRO) with a $q$-norm ambiguity set ($q$-DRO) satisfies the axioms of Positivity, Symmetry, and Order Preservation, while relaxing the rigid Ratio Preservation axiom characterizing Laplace smoothing. In this paper, we observe that Symmetry itself imposes a strong constraint: it forces all unobserved categories to receive identical probability regardless of their relation to observed categories. Motivated by this observation, we study DRO with an optimal transport ambiguity set (OT-DRO), which incorporates inter-category dissimilarities through a cost matrix and thereby enables structure-respecting smoothing. We derive a tractable dual reformulation of OT-DRO as an empirical cross-entropy minimization with a Lipschitz-type penalty on the log-probability vector, and we identify an explicit threshold on the robustness radius at which the optimal estimator reduces to the uniform distribution, paralleling the threshold established for $q$-DRO. We then show, through Sion's minimax theorem, that DRO for probability smoothing over any compact convex ambiguity set that contains a strictly positive distribution is equivalent to entropy maximization over that set. This unifying perspective explains the parallel threshold structure in $q$-DRO and OT-DRO.

Optimization and Control.title: Fully First-Order Optimization for Implicit Multilevel Compositions via Recursive Perturbations
Optimization and Control.summary: We study optimization over a finite composition of implicit response maps generated by smooth potentials with strongly monotone signed gradients. This class includes chains mixing strongly convex minimization and strongly convex--strongly concave saddle responses. We propose a fully first-order method based on recursively perturbed response solves. The central issue is stability under inexact response solves: a downstream adjoint error changes the perturbation vector of the next upstream perturbed problem. We establish coupled bounds for the forward response errors and backward errors in the scaled response differences whose coefficients remain bounded as the perturbation parameter $δ$ decreases. A triangular Lyapunov construction combines these bounds with the $O(δ)$ bias of the exact perturbation estimator. For the warm-started method with finitely many inner iterations, this gives $\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\|\nablaΦ(x^k)\|^2 \leq O(K^{-1})+O(δ^2).$ Thus, for fixed problem data and finite depth, $δ=O(ε)$ yields an $O(ε^{-2})$ outer-iteration dependence. For strongly convex minimization chains, we also derive condition-number-dependent first-order oracle complexity bounds.

Optimization and Control.title: The Principle of Optimality in Dynamic Programming: A Pedagogical Note
Optimization and Control.summary: The principle of optimality is a fundamental aspect of dynamic programming, which states that the optimal solution to a dynamic optimization problem can be found by combining the optimal solutions to its sub-problems. While this principle is generally applicable, it is often only taught for problems with finite or countable state spaces in order to sidestep measure-theoretic complexities. Therefore, it cannot be applied to classic models such as inventory management and dynamic pricing models that have continuous state spaces, and students may not be aware of the possible challenges involved in studying dynamic programming models with general state spaces. To address this, we provide conditions and a self-contained simple proof that establish when the principle of optimality for discounted dynamic programming is valid. These conditions shed light on the difficulties that may arise in the general state space case. We provide examples from the literature that include the relatively involved case of universally measurable dynamic programming and the simple case of finite dynamic programming where our main result can be applied to show that the principle of optimality holds.

Optimization and Control.title: Computing Fréchet Means on Unknown Submanifolds of Riemannian Manifolds
Optimization and Control.summary: Empirical averages are fundamental statistical primitives. On nonlinear spaces, their generalization, the Fréchet mean, generally lacks a closed-form solution, and its computation requires solving an optimization problem. We study the computation of intrinsic Fréchet means for data supported on an unknown compact $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $M_{1}$ embedded in an ambient metric space $(X,d_{\operatorname{obs}})$. Such settings arise when observations are better represented in non-Euclidean spaces, like probability distributions in Wasserstein space. We assume access only to a local sampler on $M_{1}$ and the observation metric $d_{\operatorname{obs}}$, without knowledge of its intrinsic geometry. We propose a graph-based iterative algorithm that adaptively samples the manifold and approximates geodesic interpolation. Under mild assumptions, we establish an $O(1/T)$ expected objective gap guarantee using at most $\widetilde{O}(T^{4d+3})$ sampled points. As a byproduct of our analysis we extend the metric equivalence guarantees of ISOMAP from Euclidean to Riemannian ambient spaces, which may be of independent interest. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method for computing intrinsic averages on unknown data manifolds.

Optimization and Control.title: A note on the complexity of random subspace model-based methods for derivative-free optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We demonstrate that, with a suitable rescaling, using Johnson-Lindenstrauss transforms (JLTs) in the random subspace model-based derivative-free optimization (DFO) algorithm from [Cartis & Roberts, Math. Prog. 199 (2023)] achieves an improved first-order worst-case evaluation complexity bound compared to 'unscaled' JLTs. This improved bound does not require any modification to the original algorithm or complexity analysis, and matches the best-known bound in terms of dimension dependence for model-based DFO (e.g. achieved by [Scheinberg & Chaudhry, ICM 2026] using Haar matrices in a similar framework). A similarly refined analysis of the analogous second-order subspace method from [Cartis & Roberts, Opt. Meth. & Softw. (2026)] shows that using suitably scaled JLTs to generate the subspaces gives a better complexity bound, which improves over full-space methods only if the problem has low effective rank.

Optimization and Control.title: Quantitative convergence for displacement monotone Mean Field Games of control
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper we establish quantitative convergence results for both open and closed-loop Nash equilibria of N-player stochastic differential games in the setting of Mean Field Games of Controls (MFGC), a class of models where interactions among agents occur through both states and controls. Our analysis covers a general class of non-separable Hamiltonians satisfying a displacement monotonicity condition, along with mild regularity and growth conditions at infinity. A major novelty of our work is the rigorous treatment of a nontrivial fixed-point problem on a space of measures, which arises naturally in the MFGC formulation. Unlike prior works that either restrict to separable Hamiltonians - rendering the fixed-point map trivial - or assume convergence or regularity properties of the fixed point map, we develop a detailed structural analysis of this equation and its N-player analogue. This leads to new regularity results for the fixed-point maps and, in turn, to quantitative convergence of open-loop equilibria. We further derive sharp a priori estimates for the N-player Nash system, enabling us to control the discrepancy between open and closed-loop strategies, and thus to conclude the convergence of closed-loop equilibria. Our framework also accommodates common noise in a natural way.

Optimization and Control.title: Stability and Stabilization of Kronecker-Sum-Coupled Multilinear Systems
Optimization and Control.summary: Coupled dynamical systems with multi-dimensional state structures arise in many applications such as spatiotemporal processes and large-scale interconnected systems. However, existing studies primarily focus on matrix-based coupled systems or tensor-based dynamical systems without couplings. The properties of coupled tensor-based systems remain largely unexplored. In this article, we study Kronecker-sum-coupled multilinear systems under the transform-based tensor product framework. We establish fundamental tensor spectral properties showing that stability can be characterized through lower-dimensional subsystem dynamics together with slice-wise matrix stability in the transform domain. We further develop optimization conditions for state-feedback stabilization and show that the stabilization problem can be decomposed into independent subsystem problems. Finally, we analyze the computational complexity of the proposed framework and demonstrate its substantial computational advantages over unfolding-based approaches using both synthetic systems and multi-inertia motor systems.

Optimization and Control.title: Partially Adaptive Robust Optimization for Uncertain Fluid Processing Networks
Optimization and Control.summary:
This paper studies the problem of controlling fluid approximations of processing networks under uncertainty. Classical robust formulations for such models rely on static (here-and-now) control decisions that must remain feasible for all realizations of uncertainty, often leading to highly conservative solutions. We propose a partially adaptive robust optimization framework that incorporates observed system information into the control policy at the planning point, enabling less conservative and more responsive decisions while retaining worst-case guarantees.
  Our approach begins by modeling the fluid network dynamics as a Separated Continuous Linear Program (SCLP) in the server-effort formulation. We introduce continuous-time extensions of the budgeted uncertainty set and develop three families of uncertainty structures appropriate for fluid-flow systems. For each family, we derive the corresponding robust counterpart. Since these robust counterparts include uncertainty in the objective, they cannot be solved directly by the classical SCLP--Simplex method.
  To address this challenge, we develop a hybrid algorithm that integrates an extended SCLP framework with the Saddle-Point Frank--Wolfe (SP--FW) method. This hybrid approach combines tractable continuous-time optimization with efficient saddle-point updates, yielding feasible and near-optimal partially adaptive robust solutions. The resulting methodology advances robust fluid control by enabling uncertainty-aware, dynamically informed decision policies while preserving computational tractability.

Optimization and Control.title: Second-order geometry of optimal transport: cost identifiability and stability
Optimization and Control.summary:
We study the optimal transport value as a functional of the ground cost. Although this functional is an infimum of linear functionals and is therefore polyhedral for finitely supported marginals, it develops genuine second-order geometry in the smooth continuous setting. Under twist, nondegeneracy, and regularity assumptions, we prove twice differentiability with respect to the cost in Hölder spaces, derive a variational formula for the Hessian, and characterize its null space. The resulting curvature is strict transverse to the cost perturbations that preserve the observed optimal plan.
  This structure yields identifiability and quantitative stability for inverse optimal transport. For bilinear costs $c_A(x,y)=-x^\top Ay$, a full spanning condition on the Hessians of the Kantorovich potential implies that every nonzero matrix compatible with a single optimal coupling is a positive multiple of the true matrix. We show that this condition can be attained by arbitrarily small compactly supported smooth perturbations of the transport potential that preserve the target marginal's support and density class. For $d\ge2$, uniquely optimal discrete plans and same-base elliptical models, including Gaussians, retain nontrivial degeneracies. Finally, we quantify the regularization bias and sampling error of entropic inverse optimal transport as the regularization parameter vanishes. Thus the second-order geometry of the forward transport problem provides a means towards identifiability, stability, and statistical cost recovery.

Optimization and Control.title: TIGER: Tunable-Geometry Accelerated Gradient Sliding with Adaptive Safeguards under Similarity
Optimization and Control.summary: We study distributed composite optimization under function similarity when synchronized gradient queries dominate local computation. We propose TIGER, an accelerated gradient-sliding method in problem-adapted Bregman geometry. The method applies to constrained non-Euclidean domains, allows the communicated correction term to be nonconvex, and terminates each local subproblem using a computable stationarity residual. Each iteration reuses one synchronized correction gradient during the local solve and makes a second query to construct the composite subgradient for the mirror step. Under relative strong convexity and cocoercivity of the stabilized model error, the communication complexity is $O((1+\sqrt{δ_ω/μ})\log(1/\varepsilon))$, where $μ$ is the relative strong-convexity parameter and $δ_ω$ is a geometry-adjusted similarity parameter. The analysis recovers the Hessian-similarity rate in Hilbert geometry and provides an explicit finite bound on $δ_ω$ in entropy geometry on a truncated simplex. We also introduce Adaptive TIGER, which selects the stabilization coefficient and the similarity estimate during the run. Under uniform backtracking bounds, the adaptive method has the same asymptotic communication order as fixed-parameter TIGER, including the queries spent on backtracking. Numerical experiments compare Adaptive TIGER with several applicable first-order methods on entropic Wasserstein barycenter problems using the Fashion-MNIST dataset.

Optimization and Control.title: Acceleration of Generalized Conditional Gradient Methods
Optimization and Control.summary: We develop an adaptive acceleration of generalized conditional gradient methods for convex objectives with a strongly convex regularizer. A computable primal--dual residual certifies Lyapunov decrease without evaluating the regularizer or any Hessian. Each iteration accepts a balanced accelerated trial when the residual is nonpositive; otherwise it takes a mirror-descent step with doubling backtracking and sets the auxiliary parameter explicitly from the dual decrease and the stopping gap. Under uniform strong-convexity and smoothness bounds on the relevant sublevel set, the method converges globally at a linear rate. Near a nondegenerate minimizer, balanced trials pass above a fixed curvature threshold. The adaptive curvature updates then guarantee a positive fraction of accelerated steps and a local accelerated rate. The method applies directly to entropically regularized Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto (JKO) steps whose energies contain nonlocal interaction terms with nondiagonal Hessians. Experiments on JKO steps for granular media and for Poisson--Nernst--Planck systems, in one and three dimensions, show that the method reduces both oracle calls and computing time by a large fraction compared with generalized conditional gradient methods with fixed or adaptive step sizes.

Optimization and Control.title: On the Role of Batch Size in Stochastic Conditional Gradient Methods
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the role of batch size in stochastic conditional gradient methods under a $μ$-Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz ($μ$-KL) condition. Focusing on momentum-based stochastic conditional gradient algorithms (e.g., Scion), we derive a new analysis that explicitly captures the interaction between stepsize, batch size, and stochastic noise. Our study reveals a regime-dependent behavior: increasing the batch size initially improves optimization accuracy but, beyond a critical threshold, the benefits saturate and can eventually degrade performance under a fixed token budget. Notably, the theory predicts the magnitude of the optimal stepsize and aligns well with empirical practices observed in large-scale training. Leveraging these insights, we derive principled guidelines for selecting the batch size and stepsize, and propose an adaptive strategy that increases batch size and sequence length during training while preserving convergence guarantees. Experiments on NanoGPT are consistent with the theoretical predictions and illustrate the emergence of the predicted scaling regimes. Overall, our results provide a theoretical framework for understanding batch size scaling in stochastic conditional gradient methods and offer guidance for designing efficient training schedules in large-scale optimization.

Optimization and Control.title: Observability of wave equations with time- and space-dependent potentials: a counterexample under GCC and a positive criterion on the disk
Optimization and Control.summary:
We show that the geometric control condition (GCC) for the free wave equation does not guarantee internal observability in the presence of a smooth time-dependent potential. On a bounded connected domain with analytic boundary, we construct a nonempty open observation set such that the pair satisfies GCC and the free Dirichlet wave is observable, and a smooth $2π$-periodic potential for which there exists a nonzero smooth Dirichlet wave that vanishes on the observed cylinder for all time. The wave is the unique mild solution in the space $X_Ω=L^2(Ω)\times H^{-1}(Ω)$ on every finite interval, so no finite observation horizon yields an observability inequality for this fixed potential. The construction starts from a real-valued local counterexample to unique continuation across a noncharacteristic hyperplane; this local statement is of independent interest, since earlier constructions for the wave operator use complex-valued waves and potentials. The global counterexample is obtained by joining flat oscillatory solutions along the edges of a polygonal observation set, repairing their sum at the vertices without changing its zero set, and then using a spatial transition to a common time-independent pair near the boundary.
  For comparison, on the unit disk we show that an observation region containing a central disk and a neighborhood of an embedded cross-cut yields observability for every weak wave at sufficiently large observation time, with constants uniform over bounded measurable potentials; the proof uses a cut, logarithmic polar coordinates, and a Carleman weight whose favorable flux is confined to the observed artificial boundary.

Optimization and Control.title: Variance Reduction Note 2: The Convergence of SPIDER
Optimization and Control.summary: The stochastic path-integrated differential estimator (SPIDER) tracks a gradient by accumulating small, shared-sample gradient differences and periodically refreshing the estimate. This second expository note on recursive variance reduction explains SPIDER-SFO and gives a self-contained proof of its expected first-order stationarity guarantee. The argument combines an epochwise mean-square error bound with descent under a clipped, normalized update. It yields $O(ε^{-3})$ stochastic gradient evaluations in the online setting and $O(n+\sqrt n\,ε^{-2})$ component gradient evaluations for a finite sum, with the remaining problem parameters fixed. All refresh costs are included. The presentation is pedagogical and makes no claim of a new algorithm or convergence rate.

Optimization and Control.title: Variance Reduction for Stochastic Switching in Functionally Constrained Federated Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: Federated learning (FL) is increasingly used in safety-critical and fairness-sensitive applications, where learning objectives must be optimized subject to functional constraints. This setting is challenging due to costly projection onto the resulting feasible set, stochastic constraint information, partial client participation, and limited communication at edge devices. We propose a federated stochastic switching framework based on primal-only updates, avoiding dual-variable tuning for functionally constrained federated optimization. For convex objectives, the framework further supports compression with error feedback to control compression-induced bias. We establish high-probability convergence and feasibility guarantees under stochastic gradients and partial client participation, and extend the analysis to weakly convex objectives through proximal-stationarity guarantees. Our bounds isolate the effects of stochastic gradients, constraint-evaluation noise, and partial participation, and show that direct switching can retain a nonvanishing constraint-estimation error even with exact local constraint evaluations. To overcome this limitation, we develop variance-reducing constraint estimators that yield vanishing feasibility and stationarity guarantees with fixed per-round client participation and constraint-evaluation batch sizes. Experiments on Neyman-Pearson classification, fairness-constrained learning on the ADULT dataset, and constrained deep reinforcement learning demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

Optimization and Control.title: Semidefinite programming bounds for distance distribution of spherical codes
Optimization and Control.summary: Multipoint semidefinite programming bounds for spherical codes use polynomials in several variables. We show how to obtain bounds for the distance distribution using a polynomial of one variable on a prescribed interval. The multivariate SDP supplies the required positivity; the sign and size of the univariate polynomial reveal the geometric consequences. We prove three- and four-point reductions and explain how to choose the polynomial to bound the number of pairs in a prescribed interval. Three-point experiments in dimension four illustrate this procedure, including nearly antipodal pairs, intervals near inner product $1/2$, and a local approach to the kissing number bound. As a further application, we extract a degree-six polynomial from the exact four-point construction of de Laat, Leijenhorst, and de Muinck Keizer. Its sign and four zeros give a direct description of the distance restriction underlying uniqueness of the $24$-cell.

Optimization and Control.title: An optimal inequality between nonlinear eigenvalues in convex sets
Optimization and Control.summary: Let $λ_p(Ω)$ be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the $p$-Laplacian in a bounded convex open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^N$, $N\ge2$. We prove that $p\mapstoλ_p(Ω)^{1/p}/π_p$ is strictly decreasing, where $π_p^p$ is the first eigenvalue on the unit interval. Consequently, for $1<q<p<\infty$, the sharp upper bound for $λ_p(Ω)^{1/p}/λ_q(Ω)^{1/q}$ is $π_p/π_q$. This bound is not attained and is approached by slabs, resolving the conjecture on the supremum formulated in the plane by Parini (J. Convex Anal. 2017). The proof combines log-concavity of the first eigenfunction with a vector field constructed from the one-dimensional eigenfunctions. The endpoint limits recover the Hersch--Protter and reverse Cheeger (or Buser) inequalities.

Optimization and Control.title: A noncommunicative Kalman condition for null controllability of backward stochastic parabolic systems
Optimization and Control.summary: We study null controllability of backward stochastic heat systems with constant couplings in both the state and the martingale integrand, common scalar diffusion, and a localized drift control. We prove that null controllability is equivalent to a noncommutative word-rank condition on the two coupling matrices and the control matrix. The proof combines a factorization of the dual dynamics, positivity and small-time coercivity of a finite-dimensional stochastic Gramian, and a Lebeau--Robbiano spectral argument. Failure of the rank condition yields an invariant unobservable subspace.

Optimization and Control.title: Directional Fineness for Radiant and Co-Radiant Sets: Separation and Quantitative Approximation
Optimization and Control.summary:
A prescribed directionally fine family of cones yields separation and primal bipolar identities for closed radiant and co-radiant sets in real normed spaces. Positive levels of adapted positively homogeneous functions separate points from closed radiant sets, while a correction by the norm provides bounded radiant neighbourhoods for co-radiant separation. The resulting classes also calibrate radial thresholds and represent gauges and cogauges through strict separators. For convex directionally fine families, the separating generators can be chosen Lipschitz and superlinear, yielding convex separating superlevels.
  Closed co-radiant sets with compact direction sets admit finite relative outer approximations by positive superlevels of selected generators, with separation preservation and directional and bounded-section error estimates, without requiring continuity or boundedness of the radial profile. Superlinear generators yield a global residual error bound, exact penalization for Lipschitz objectives, recovery estimates, and convergence of bounded approximate minimizers.
  An explicit convex directionally fine axial family is available in every real normed space. Its norm-corrected functions realize separation and bipolarity without rotundity assumptions, while an axial recovery map improves the relative distance factor from $η/(1-η)$ to $η$. A three-ray production model illustrates the quantitative recovery estimates.

Optimization and Control.title: Non-Acceleration of the Heavy-Ball Method in 1D
Optimization and Control.summary: Despite having an asymptotically optimal rate of convergence on convex quadratics, the acceleration of Polyak's heavy-ball method and a characterization of its dynamics within more general settings have remained long standing open problems. Recently, the work of Goujaud et al. [Math. Program. (2025)] made progress regarding acceleration in the context of smooth, strongly convex minimization: for a small enough inverse condition number, either the method does not accelerate on quadratics, or there exists a smooth strongly convex function such that heavy-ball cycles over the roots of unity. The constructed functions have two variables, thus leaving the question of acceleration over univariate functions open. In this work, we use a Fourier-based analysis to i) provide a proof for the non-acceleration of the heavy-ball method over the class of univariate smooth strongly convex functions. We also ii) provide a strict enlargement of the previous root-of-unity cycling region, with insights regarding the "fractional" sets of Goujaud et al. [arXiv:2502.19916], and iii) give a higher dimensional cycling instance which is not covered by root-of-unity cycling.

Optimization and Control.title: Learning-Based Spectrum Cartography in Low Earth Orbit Satellite Networks: A Survey
Optimization and Control.summary: Low earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks are emerging as important infrastructure for global connectivity and space-based sensing, while their rapidly varying geometry, heterogeneous measurements, and dynamic propagation environments create challenges for acquiring and exploiting spatial radio information. Spectrum cartography provides a framework for constructing and updating spatial representations of radio conditions from sparse observations. This survey reviews learning-based spectrum cartography for LEO satellite networks from an integrated inference--decision perspective. We organize the literature around three representative task categories: radio map reconstruction, localization and state estimation, and map-informed resource allocation. We further examine the progression from classical interpolation, statistical estimation, and structured optimization toward learning-based approaches that exploit environmental context, relational structure, generative modeling, and adaptive information fusion. Particular attention is given to attention mechanisms for learning query- and context-dependent interactions among irregular observations, while distinguishing learned relevance from calibrated measurement reliability. Representative formulations and illustrative examples clarify these modeling principles. Finally, we synthesize cross-cutting lessons and identify open challenges in uncertainty modeling, generalization, dynamic map updating, scalable inference, realistic evaluation, and tighter coupling between radio-map inference and network decision making.

Optimization and Control.title: $\varepsilon$-$\mathcal{VU}$ spaces and approximate leaves\\ for sublinear composite functions
Optimization and Control.summary: Let \(h\) be proper, closed and sublinear, and let \(F\) be of class \(C^1\). The exact \(\mathcal{VU}\) calculus of the composite \(f=h\circ F\) is taken as known. This paper studies enlargements \(\bar\partial_\varepsilon h\subset\partial_\varepsilon h\) and the resulting \(\varepsilon\)-spaces of \(f\). Nested inclusions give one-sided Painlevé--Kuratowski limits of \(\mathcal{V}_\varepsilon\) and \(\mathcal{U}_\varepsilon\) at points of the lineality space \(\mathcal{U}h(0)\). An additional transversality transfers those limits through \(F\); without it only the exact chain rule is available. Approximate leaves \(\mathcal{M}_\varepsilon(x)=F^{-1}\bigl(F(x)+\mathcal{U}_\varepsilon h(F(x))\bigr)\) are inner semicontinuous under the nesting \(\mathcal{U}h(F(\bar x))\subset\mathcal{U}_\varepsilon h(F(x))\). For a polyhedral outer function the activity set freezes along the exact leaf for small \(\varepsilon\), so the dimension identity holds on that leaf and not necessarily in a full neighbourhood of \((\bar x,0)\). Partial smoothness of \(h\) relative to \(\mathcal{U}h(0)\) extends a known result from the origin to the lineality space; it is not used by the transfer theorems.

Optimization and Control.title: Dynamic Quantum-Assisted Co-Design of Controller and Lyapunov Candidate Parameters for Nonlinear Systems
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper proposes a dynamic quantum-assisted co-design framework for nonlinear closed-loop systems in which controller parameters and Lyapunov candidate parameters are redesigned jointly at successive decision epochs. Unlike conventional nonlinear control designs that typically tune controller gains offline and perform stability analysis separately, the proposed method embeds performance improvement and sample-based Lyapunov verification within a unified online optimization loop. The main novelty is a two-step computational structure that first contracts the continuous admissible search region around the current operating condition using a Black-Hole calibration procedure and then constructs a finite binary representation only over this calibrated region. The encoded objective is obtained from sampled nonlinear closed-loop evaluations and approximated by a local quadratic pseudo-Boolean surrogate, enabling an Ising-type Hamiltonian representation suitable for quantum-assisted optimization. Quantum imaginary time evolution is then used to explore the encoded Hamiltonian, and the resulting candidate bitstrings are decoded into continuous controller and Lyapunov parameters. To reduce dependence on the surrogate model, the decoded candidates are re-evaluated using the original nonlinear closed-loop cost and Lyapunov penalties before the final update is applied. The framework can accommodate sampled forms of different Lyapunov decay specifications by modifying the corresponding penalty and is numerically evaluated on first-order nonlinear consensus, second-order nonlinear consensus, and induction motor drive control examples. The implementation code used to generate the reported results is available at \href{https://github.com/LSU-RAISE-LAB/DQCLS-NS}{GitHub}.

Optimization and Control.title: Globally Optimal Estimation of Nested Logit Models
Optimization and Control.summary: Nested logit is widely used in operational demand models, yet jointly estimating its utility coefficients and nest dissimilarity parameters requires nonconvex optimization. Standard estimation routines offer no certificate of global optimality, leaving a gap between globally optimizing decisions under nested-logit demand and reliably estimating that demand model. We develop, to our knowledge, the first globally convergent optimization framework with an explicit global-accuracy guarantee for joint nested-logit estimation. Our central complexity result confines all exponential dependence to the number of free nest dissimilarity parameters: computation is polynomial in the numbers of observations, alternatives, and utility coefficients. Consequently, under the stated compact-domain and relaxation-error conditions, fixing the number of nests yields an additive polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS). The framework exploits an exact exponential-cone formulation for fixed dissimilarities and a spatial branch-and-bound algorithm that searches only over the free dissimilarities. Valid likelihood bounds provide an anytime certificate and finite termination at any prescribed additive average-log-likelihood tolerance. Across eight benchmark datasets and 240 estimation instances, the method certifies every reported solution and exposes inferior local estimates despite normal solver termination. These results establish a computational foundation for globally certified nested-logit estimation.

Optimization and Control.title: Pareto optimality under nondegeneracy at infinity
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we consider a broad class of multiobjective optimization problems, which are defined in a simple and elegant manner by using only two basic notions of Newton polyhedra and nondegeneracy at infinity associated with given data. For each problem in the class, its several basic properties are studied; in particular, necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of (weakly/properly) efficient solutions as well as the Hölder-type global weak sharp minima are established.

Optimization and Control.title: Hodge-Carleman estimates and global attractors for heterogeneous elastic waves with localized damping on Riemannian manifolds
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the long-time dynamics of the semilinear Lamé system of isotropic elasticity on a compact Riemannian manifold with boundary, for a heterogeneous medium whose density and Lamé moduli vary in space, under a frictional dissipation which acts only on an open set $ω$. The elastic operator is the divergence of the Hooke stress tensor, and the starting point is a structural identity which shows that the dilatation and the vorticity of the displacement satisfy wave equations with the pressure and the shear speeds, respectively, coupled to the displacement only through first-order terms. A single weight function, free of critical points and strictly convex with respect to the two ray metrics of the medium, then serves for the displacement, its dilatation and its vorticity alike, and this Hodge structure yields Carleman estimates for the Lamé operator with variable coefficients at two energy levels, provided that $ω$ contains a neighbourhood of the boundary and that such a weight exists on the undamped region. The hypothesis is fulfilled on every compact manifold with boundary by damping regions of arbitrarily small volume. From these estimates we derive unique continuation for elastic waves with bounded, merely measurable, time-dependent potentials and an internal observability inequality, which in turn yield, for subcritical restoring forces in dimension three, a compact global attractor which coincides with the unstable manifold of the equilibria, has finite fractal dimension and is bounded in $(H^2\cap H^1_0)\times H^1_0$, together with a generalized exponential attractor.
